title: Garden and Wild Plants
seo_title: Year 1 Science: Garden and Wild Plants Worksheets (Naming Plants)
standard_text: Identify and name a variety of common wild and garden plants, including deciduous and evergreen trees.
meta_desc: Free Year 1 science worksheets on garden and wild plants: naming common flowers and weeds, plants that sting, and a plant hunt with a bar chart. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Garden plants are planted by people. Look, but do not eat wild plants.
body_html:
How to think about it

Some plants are wild. Some grow in gardens.

  • Wild plants grow by themselves, like daisies and dandelions.
  • Garden plants are planted by people, like roses.
  • Look, but do not eat wild plants.
Example

A dandelion: wild or garden?

It grows by itself

Answer: wild

Example

Which plant stings?

Leaves with tiny hairs

Answer: a stinging nettle

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all flowers are planted by people.
  • Thinking a weed is not a plant.
  • Thinking it is safe to eat any berry.

faq.q: What is the difference between wild and garden plants?
faq.a: Wild plants grow by themselves, like daisies and dandelions. Garden plants are usually planted by people, like roses and sunflowers.

faq.q: Which common wild plants should Year 1 know?
faq.a: Daisies, dandelions, buttercups, clover, stinging nettles, thistles and poppies.

faq.q: Is it safe to touch wild plants?
faq.a: Look carefully. Stinging nettles sting and some berries are poisonous, so never eat wild plants and wash your hands afterwards.
